review_scope: Technical review of 23 paired surfaces and the separate installed near and far F02 lighting proof. Human play and artistic acceptance are tracked separately.

images.observation: Table and work light pool still read against the far doorway. The companion sits slightly farther right in this frame.
The lamp footprint and tile joints stay visible beside the curtain.
The resident, desk and radiator remain visible across the warm room.
The desk, radiator, cabinet and window keep their depth under the ceiling light.
The wall beam, sill and fitted worktops remain visible. The edge of the rough reflection moves between captures.
The machine face, piping, floor and subdued basement lighting remain visible.
The books and shelf openings retain separation against the door and oak floor.
The tiled corners and pipe cover remain legible, with a change in local exposure.
The nearly black recess retains brick courses and mortar contrast.
The open leaf and electrical components remain legible in the pools of light.
The brass rail, tiled stair and den remain visible.
The low booth light continues to show the seated patron and wall trim.
Beam, trim, framed pictures and local accents remain visible.
Letter slots and brass faceplates retain separation from the dark wood.
The radiator fins and window slats remain distinct. There is modest intensity variation across the wall.
The railings and both stair header lights retain contrast at the roof hatch.
The tank silhouette and city horizon remain both readable.
The terminal and signal-board finish remain intact. Their shadow edge moves slightly between frames.
The bypass cover, neighboring fitting and tile grid remain visible.
The floor spill and radiator still sit within the intended lamp pool.
The installed wet shapes retain volume and contact shadows. The handheld light falls more narrowly beside the chair in this frame.
Toaster and counter stock remain distinct with the crumbs present.
The watch station keeps its outline and wall contact. The rim of the pool varies between captures.
